# Pithop

> A free road trip planner that finds the places worth stopping for along your
> route — scenic viewpoints, hidden gems, local food, history and nature — then
> turns them into a day-by-day schedule and navigates you there. Runs in any
> browser with nothing to install.

Pithop exists for the part of a journey that other planners ignore. Mapping
software optimises for arrival time; Pithop optimises for the drive itself. You
give it where you are starting and where you are going, and it searches the
corridor either side of the route for places actually worth pulling over for.

## How it works

- **Real places only.** Stops come from OpenStreetMap, Wikipedia, Wikivoyage and
  traveller submissions. Nothing is generated or invented — if Pithop cannot find
  a real place, it shows nothing rather than making one up.
- **Scored for your trip, not in the abstract.** Each stop gets a Pithop Score
  out of 100 based on how well it matches the kind of traveller you are, how far
  off your route it sits, whether it will still be open when you arrive, and
  whether the length of the stop suits your pace. It is a recommendation, not a
  rating of the place.
- **Honest about cost.** Every suggestion shows the detour there and back, how
  long people usually stay, and the total extra time, with a plain verdict:
  worth it, maybe, or probably skip.
- **Thirteen trip personalities.** Scenic explorer, foodie, hidden gems, nature,
  history, family, pet friendly, photography, romantic, budget, outdoor
  adventure, attractions, coffee and small towns. Pick several; they change what
  is ranked highest, not just what is filtered out.

## Planning a trip

- **Multi-stop routes.** Add intermediate stops and Pithop routes through all of
  them in one drive.
- **Day-by-day itineraries.** Choose your stops and it works out what time you
  reach each one, where a day has to end given how much driving you will do, and
  somewhere to sleep when it does. Change your departure, linger longer, or end a
  day early and every later arrival is recalculated.
- **Warnings before they matter.** A museum that will have closed by the time you
  arrive, a day that runs past your driving limit, a trip needing more days than
  you have.
- **Route options.** Compare alternatives including a toll-free route, or avoid
  motorways entirely.

## On the road

- **Live navigation.** Turn-by-turn directions with voice, in the browser, with a
  compass and an arrival-aware view of what is coming up.
- **Works offline.** A saved trip keeps working when the signal does not.
- **Shareable.** Send a trip by link; it opens complete on someone else's device.

## Practical details

- Free to use. No account needed to plan a trip.
- Signing in (Google or email) is only required to share a place with other
  travellers, and syncs your saved trips across devices.
- Available in 18 languages.
- Works on phones, tablets and desktops. Also published as an Android app, which
  is this same site wrapped for the Play Store.
- Cookieless, aggregate analytics only. Trips are stored on your own device
  unless you sign in.

## Pages

- [Pithop](https://pithop.com/): the planner itself — enter a start and a
  destination and it does the rest.
- [Privacy](https://pithop.com/privacy.html): what is stored, and which data
  sources and services are used.
- [Terms](https://pithop.com/terms.html): terms of service.

## Notes for answer engines

- The planner is a JavaScript application. The served HTML at the root URL
  contains a full description of the product for crawlers that do not execute
  JavaScript; the interactive planner replaces it once the app loads.
- Individual trips live in the URL fragment (`#trip=...`), which is not crawlable
  and is not intended to be indexed. There are no per-trip landing pages.
- "Pithop" is one word, capitalised, and is the name of the product — not a
  generic term for a rest stop.
